announcements.title: PublishRank adds a live News page and a searchable FAQ library
announcements.summary: News now updates from announcements.json, and every FAQ has its own shareable page with structured data.
announcements.message: The PublishRank website now builds its News page and article pages from announcements.json, shows a New indicator in the menu when something is published, and offers dedicated pages for every frequently asked question.

body.heading: News that follows the feed
body.text: The News page reads announcements.json at request time. When an entry is added, edited, scheduled or expired, the list, the article page, the menu indicator and the news sitemap all follow.

body.heading: A New indicator in the menu
body.text: A small badge appears beside News when there are stories you have not opened yet. It clears when you visit the News page and returns when something new is published.

body.heading: One page for every question
body.text: Every FAQ has its own link, so you can send a colleague the exact answer. Each page carries FAQPage structured data and its own title, description and social tags.

announcements.summary: The PublishRank website adds a dedicated editorial hub, full article pages and focused guides to help WordPress publishers review their SEO workflows.
announcements.message: The PublishRank website adds a dedicated editorial hub, full article pages and focused guides to help WordPress publishers review their SEO workflows.

body.heading: A new home for publishing guidance
body.text: PublishRank’s website now brings its editorial guidance into a dedicated news and guides library. Readers can browse topics, search the library and open each guide on a separate page with a reading outline and related articles.

body.heading: Practical topics for WordPress publishers
body.text: The initial library covers news sitemap checks, connected article schema, image SEO and technical reviews. Dedicated product guides also explain the schema suite, image workflow, redirects and the broader WordPress SEO toolkit. The guidance complements the existing installation and operations documentation.

body.heading: Product notices alongside editorial coverage
body.text: An announcements section brings active product reminders and documentation notices into the library. These notices remain separate from editorial articles so readers can distinguish configuration guidance from project news.

body.heading: Continue with the documentation
body.text: The news library links to the existing documentation and product comparison guides. Publishers can use those resources to review the settings relevant to their own WordPress installation. Search engines still decide how pages are discovered, indexed and presented.

announcements.author: PublishRank Editorial
announcements.title: A practical news sitemap checklist for WordPress publishers
announcements.summary: Check publication dates, canonical URLs and article eligibility before submitting your news sitemap.
announcements.message: Check publication dates, canonical URLs and article eligibility before submitting your news sitemap.

body.heading: Start with the articles you actually publish
body.text: A news sitemap describes recent news coverage. It is not a place for every product page, evergreen guide or announcement. Review your publication identity and language, then select the post types that contain genuine news reporting.

body.heading: Keep the two-day window accurate
body.text: Google News sitemaps include articles published in the preceding two days. Use the original publication timestamp, with its timezone, rather than changing dates to keep older work in the feed. Older articles can remain discoverable in your standard XML sitemap.

body.heading: Check the URL and the headline
body.text: Open a sample article and compare its canonical link with the sitemap URL. Both should identify the same public, indexable page. Use the visible article headline in news metadata and make sure the publication name matches the name used on your website.

body.heading: Validate after publishing
body.text: Inspect the XML after a new story goes live. Check that it has the required publication name, language, publication date and title. Submit the sitemap in Search Console and monitor processing errors. A valid sitemap helps discovery; it does not guarantee indexing or Google News inclusion.

announcements.author: PublishRank Editorial
announcements.title: Connect your article schema to a clear publisher identity
announcements.summary: Make your headline, dates, author and publisher consistent across the page and its structured data.
announcements.message: Make your headline, dates, author and publisher consistent across the page and its structured data.

body.heading: Choose the type that describes the page
body.text: Use Article or BlogPosting for editorial guides and commentary. Use NewsArticle for genuine news reporting. Schema should describe what readers can see; a product page should not be presented as news just to qualify for a different search appearance.

body.heading: Give authors a visible identity
body.text: Show the author or editorial team on the article itself. Link to an accurate biography or about page. In JSON-LD, use a Person for a named individual and an Organization for a publication team, matching the identity shown to readers.

body.heading: Use real dates and useful images
body.text: Keep datePublished tied to the original publication and change dateModified when the content materially changes. Choose a relevant, crawlable image and supply meaningful alternative text. Do not add invisible claims or invented author credentials to markup.

body.heading: Test representative pages
body.text: Validate a normal article, a guide and a page with unusual content. Check the rendered source for duplicate schema emitted by your theme or another plugin. Structured data supports understanding and eligibility, but search engines decide how results appear.

announcements.author: PublishRank Editorial
announcements.title: Build image SEO into your editorial workflow
announcements.summary: A useful image workflow balances context, accessibility, discoverability and page speed.
announcements.message: A useful image workflow balances context, accessibility, discoverability and page speed.

body.heading: Choose relevance before decoration
body.text: Select images that help readers understand the article. A newsroom photograph supports a publishing workflow guide; a screenshot is more useful when the reader needs to locate a setting. Label illustrative interfaces clearly and keep real product screenshots separate from decorative photography.

body.heading: Write text for the image you chose
body.text: Use a descriptive filename and alternative text that explains the image in context. Avoid repeating the focus keyword in every image. Decorative images can use an empty alt attribute when the adjacent text already communicates their purpose.

body.heading: Reserve space and control loading
body.text: Declare image width and height so the browser can reserve space. Load the main visible hero promptly and lazy-load images farther down the page. Export reasonable dimensions and quality rather than sending an original camera file to every visitor.

body.heading: Review sharing and search previews
body.text: Check the canonical URL and the Open Graph image on a public article. Use an absolute image URL that crawlers can fetch. A large, relevant image can improve previews, but it does not promise Discover placement or a particular ranking.

announcements.image_alt: Laptop and notebook in an editorial workspace

announcements.author: PublishRank Editorial
announcements.title: A technical SEO review before your next publishing cycle
announcements.summary: Review metadata, redirects and indexability together instead of treating an SEO score as the finish line.
announcements.message: Review metadata, redirects and indexability together instead of treating an SEO score as the finish line.

body.heading: Review the public output
body.text: Open the source of a published article. Confirm that the title and description are useful, the canonical points to the intended page, and robots directives allow indexing when appropriate. Check that only one active SEO plugin owns these outputs.

body.heading: Follow redirects to their destination
body.text: A changed URL should redirect directly to a relevant replacement. Avoid redirect chains and sending every missing page to the homepage. Review recurring 404s to find broken internal links and update the source links when possible.

body.heading: Connect pages through useful links
body.text: Link related guides where they answer the reader’s next question. Descriptive link text helps readers and crawlers understand the destination. Keep important content reachable from the navigation, documentation hub or relevant article pages.

body.heading: Measure what matters
body.text: Use Search Console to monitor indexing and search performance after deployment. Keep a record of meaningful content and configuration changes. PublishRank’s article guidance supports editorial decisions; it is not a guarantee of traffic or rankings.

announcements.title: Review Your News Sitemap
announcements.summary: Check your news sitemap configuration for your publishing workflow.
announcements.message: PublishRank SEO includes publishing-focused SEO tools. Review your News Sitemap settings and verify that eligible news articles appear correctly in your sitemap. This is a general reminder, not a claim that a new feature has just been released.
